subject: Intermittent streaming stalls causing onboarding failures — urgent exec sync
messages:
From: Alex Tucker <alex.tucker@fluentai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-11T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Streaming responses stalling during our onboarding run

Vivek — quick heads up. Our integration tests with Redwood streaming are intermittently stalling when we hit model outputs > 800 tokens. The client sees a chunked transfer hang (no further chunks) and then a WebSocket read timeout after ~30s. We lose the session and have to restart the request — that breaks our real-time document editing feature.

Repro steps (short):
- Start a conversation that produces long output (~900-1200 tokens)
- Client receives first chunks, then silence for 25-40s
- Final chunk never arrives; connection goes to CLOSED_BY_CLIENT or read timeout depending on client

We attached a pcap and a trimmed server error log snippet. This is happening inside our staging workspaces and blocked our PM demo this morning. Can you prioritize? We’re evaluating Dedicated versus staying on hosted — this is blocking the decision.

Thanks,
Alex Tucker
Senior Platform Engineer, FluentAI
----

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tucker <alex.tucker@fluentai.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-11T18:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Streaming responses stalling during our onboarding run

Alex / Vivek — I dug into the logs attached. Initial observations:
- We see backend generation continuing for ~28–35s after the last chunk delivered to the client; trace IDs match a few of your recorded requests.
- Upstream (runtime) reports intermittent RPC retries to the batching service around the same timestamps — likely causing the KV cache to stall momentarily and stall token emission.
- Proxy layer (edge) shows keepalive timeouts at ~30s on a subset of connections; however, not all stalled traces have edge keepalive events.

What I’m recommending as immediate steps (can do within an hour):
- Turn on extended WebSocket keepalive for your staging tenant (60s) to reduce premature connection closure.
- Toggle a runtime flag to enforce shorter RPC timeouts and avoid long RPC retry backoff when the batching service is slow.

I’m attaching a trimmed error snippet in the ticket and the pcap you provided for SRE trace.

— Monica
CS Engineer, Redwood Inference
----
Attachment: streaming-error-snippet-logs.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Tucker <alex.tucker@fluentai.com>
Date: 2027-01-11T19:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Streaming responses stalling during our onboarding run

Quick technical note from runtime/SRE:
- Root cause hypothesis: intermittent RPC throttling between the request router and the batching service during high token-generation tails. That causes a stall in the generator loop and prevents the next chunk from being emitted even though the model is still computing.
- Mitigation we can toggle now: 
  * Lower the RPC retry backoff and fail faster so the generator surface can fallback to a smaller batch/solo-run path.
  * Increase edge WebSocket ping interval (keepalive) for the tenant to 60s.
  * Enable a temporary per-tenant fallback policy: if no chunk emitted for X seconds while model still running, route to a solo-worker execution that skips batch queue.

I can make the first two toggles and monitor. If we flip fallback to solo-run it may increase token costs for FluentAI but will restore reliability. Recommend we coordinate the toggle window and communicate impact.

— Marissa Cole
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Tucker <alex.tucker@fluentai.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-12T01:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Streaming responses stalling during our onboarding run

Thanks team — we enabled extended keepalive on our side but still saw two stalls overnight. I captured another pcap (attached) showing the client did not receive anything for ~38s while the server continued CPU work. This specifically affects two customers in our alpha cohort — we need a stable short-term fix and a timeline for when you can provide a durable solution.

Do you have an estimate for:
- ETA for the toggles (keepalive + retry backoff) to be applied?
- ETA to evaluate and, if needed, implement the per-tenant solo-run fallback?

This is now blocking our next onboarding demo and the PM is asking for an executive update. If this is going to take >24h we’ll need a credit/compensation conversation documented.

— Alex
